transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. We need to finalize the production message-streaming platform decision for the customer-notification service before the next integration milestone. The two finalists are KafkaCloud and StreamGrid — both passed our benchmark of 20,000 messages per second with sub-250-millisecond median delivery latency. The draft architecture recommends StreamGrid based on simpler operational setup and an initial capacity estimate of four brokers. Before I record a final decision, I'd like to hear from each of you — backend, support engineering, security, and FinOps — on any concerns or sign-offs you have. Let's start with backend.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something important before we go further. While testing the notification client's retry behavior this morning, I confirmed that the service already has a KafkaCloud-compatible producer and consumer path. This means using KafkaCloud would require only about two days of adapter cleanup, whereas moving to StreamGrid would require a new two-week client integration. I haven't updated the architecture document yet, so this wasn't reflected in the draft recommendation.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share something critical before we go further. During a customer escalation yesterday, I confirmed that three enterprise customers require notifications for each account to remain in order. KafkaCloud can guarantee that ordering using a customer_id partition key, while StreamGrid's tested mode cannot. I have not yet added this requirement to the review ticket, which is why it hasn't been part of the discussion so far.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share a critical security finding before we go further. During a data-flow review this afternoon, I confirmed that notification payloads contain phone numbers and must be stored and processed in eu-central-1. KafkaCloud offers that processing region for this service, while StreamGrid's selected tier does not. I have not filed the security architecture note yet, so this hasn't been part of the discussion so far.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share a critical FinOps finding before we go further. When I reconciled the cloud account this morning, I found that existing KafkaCloud reserved-capacity credits cover exactly six production brokers through the service's first year, while StreamGrid has no equivalent credit. The production deployment must provision all six KafkaCloud brokers, setting production_broker_count to exactly 6 to use the full reserved-capacity allocation. I have not amended the four-broker estimate in the draft architecture, which is why this hasn't been part of the discussion so far.
